answer.main_body: Japanese boundary wall with sukashi cutout
answer.evidence: The wall is depicted in pure flat front elevation. The top trim (rows 1-3) consists only of flat horizontal stripes with no top surface or coping depth visible from above, and the sukashi cutout in rows 11-13 shows a flat 2D silhouette without any interior sill depth.

answer.main_body: Japanese boundary wall section with openwork vent
answer.evidence: The entire tile is composed of flat horizontal bands (wall panels, beam, and stone base) with no foreshortened top surface or coping seen from above.

answer.main_body: Japanese boundary wall segment with sukashi aperture
answer.evidence: The entire wall segment and its sukashi opening are drawn in a flat architectural front elevation; horizontal bands across rows 1-3 are front-facing trim/molding with no top surface or roof slope visible from above.

answer.main_body: wall segment with lower vent opening
answer.evidence: The entire tile consists of flat horizontal bands spanning rows 1-14 (including a shaded cylindrical beam at rows 1-3 and stone base with a vent). There is no foreshortened top surface visible from above; the entire structure is depicted in flat front elevation.
